newsitem.title: USA: FLAG Financial Corp Q4 net flat.
newsitem.headline: FLAG Financial Corp Q4 net flat.

text.p: FLAG Financial Corpo said Friday consolidated net income was $419,000, or $0.20 per share, for the fourth quarter of 1996, versus net income of $439,000, or $0.20 per share, for the fourth quarter of 1995.

Results for the full year 1996, which included nonrecurring charges, reflected a net loss of $178,000, or $0.09 per share, versus net income of $2,026,000, or $0.93 per share for 1995. The nonrecurring items included charges totaling $2.8 million which related to a $4.5 million portfolio of equipment leases sold to the Bank through the Bennett Funding Group, Inc., as well as a special assessment to fund the Savings Association Insurance Fund ("SAIF") totaling $1,150,000. Both of the charges are discussed in more detail in prior news releases of the Company. Excluding the SAIF special assessment, pretax core income, defined as pretax income before the provision for loan losses and gains and losses on investments, loans and real estate, would have been $3.8 million in 1996, an increase of 8% from the $3.5 million earned in 1995.
The improvement in core earnings resulted from a combination of strong growth in net interest income and noninterest income. Specifically, net interest income increased 12% in
1996 from 1995 while noninterest income increased 20%. Excluding gains and losses, noninterest income growth was still strong, increasing 14%.

The Bank also maintained a strong capital level. Stockholders' equity was $20.5 million, or $10.07 per share, as of December 31, 1996. This level of equity represents a capital ratio of 9.2%, an increase from the 8.9% ratio as of December 31, 1995.

Nonperforming assets, which include the Bennett Funding leases, were $7.2 million at December 31, 1996, versus $2.2 million at December 31, 1995. Excluding Bennett Funding, nonperforming assets would have been approximately $2.6 million. Although nonperforming assets have increased, the allowance for loan losses has also increased significantly, totaling $4.3 million as of December 31, 1996, up from $1.3 million at December 31, 1995. Although there is no way to anticipate the timing or ultimate resolution of the Bennett Funding matter, the Company continues to seek full recovery of the amounts invested with and through Bennett Funding Group, Inc.
